description: Publish a Post to the brand’s Google Business Profile — the panel that appears on Google Search and Maps for the business. Text, optionally ONE PHOTO, and a call-to-action button. Google’s Posts API accepts NO VIDEO, so pass a still image. This PUBLISHES immediately and publicly on the business listing — show the user the exact text, photo and button and get an explicit yes BEFORE calling. If the account manages several listings, call list_business_locations first and pass locationId. EVENT and OFFER posts both REQUIRE a title and a start date (Google’s rule). On an OFFER, Google IGNORES the button’s link — pass redeemOnlineUrl instead. A CALL button dials the number on the listing and takes no link. Needs Google Business Profile connected (Settings > Connectors > Google Business Profile).

brand.description: WHICH BRAND this post belongs to — id or exact name from list_brands (a shared workspace: its profile id). Beats the connection's pin for THIS CALL ONLY; a name that matches no brand, or two, is REFUSED and nothing is posted.

hook.description: WHAT ANGLE this post is built on, recorded only at publish time. post_performance ranks hooks on it (a winner needs 5 posts sharing ONE hook), so pass a list_hooks id (e.g. "direct_callout", "before_after") or reuse your own wording EXACTLY across a campaign. Omit it and this post never votes on which hook works.

ideaId.description: short id of the content-plan idea this post came from

imageUrl.description: a Hermoso render image URL (or an upload_file url) to show on the Post

languageCode.description: BCP-47 language of the Post, default 'en'

link.description: the URL the button opens — not for CALL, and ignored on an OFFER

locationId.description: which listing, e.g. 'locations/123' from list_business_locations — only needed when the account manages more than one

recipe.description: the post's FORMAT id, e.g. "slideshow" or "imessage_chat" — post_performance groups by it, so reuse one id per format

redeemOnlineUrl.description: OFFER only — this is the link Google actually uses on an offer

startDate.description: YYYY-MM-DD — REQUIRED for EVENT and OFFER

subject.description: WHAT THIS POST IS ABOUT — product, feature, offer or theme (e.g. "winter coat", "free trial"). post_performance's second grouping axis: reuse the exact wording, as with hook.

summary.description: the body text of the Post

title.description: headline — REQUIRED for EVENT and OFFER

name: post_to_google_business
title: Post to Google Business Profile
